newsitem.title: UK: Singapore leads oil refinery profits to 11 mth high.
newsitem.headline: Singapore leads oil refinery profits to 11 mth high.

text.p: Refinery profit margins soared to their highest level since last May in most key regions last week, according to Reuters calculations using standard product yields.
The only exception was Rotterdam which is still just below highs set last November. The gain in profits was made despite a big jump of 64 cents a barrel in the cost of dated Brent crude.
Singapore again led the rally and appears to be tugging other regions higher, notably the Mediterranean, said oil dealers.
The Atlantic Basin regions -- Rotterdam and the U.S. Gulf Coast - have been held back slightly by sluggish gasoline demand in the West, said traders.
A complex refinery in Singapore averaged $5.97 a barrel profit last week or some 35 percent of the free-on-board price of Dubai crude.
Although those profits had slipped back to $5.78 on Friday even a less sophisticated, hydroskimming plant, averaged $2.96 a barrel last week. That loss compares to a loss of 36 cents last January.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, a barrel of Brent yielded a profit of over $3 a barrel last Monday, the higest level since last May.
The average for the whole of last week was $2.90 and levels ended at $2.46 last Friday.
Profits for the key domestic grade West Texas Intermediate (WTI) weren't quite as strong as Brent.
WTI averaged $1.62 a barrel last week, well above average losses of nearly $1 a barrel last September but under highs of well over $2 a barrel in November.
In Rotterdam fully upgrading Brent at a refinery yields an average of $2.62 a barrel last week, just under the average of $2.68 last November.
Gasoline prices struggled to make substantial gains last week in Rotterdam. But the outlook this week is better, said traders, which may boost margins.
Last Tuesday, Mediterranean margins hit their highest level since last May. But thereafter profits slipped back as crude prices gained ground.
Nevertheless, fully upgrading or complex margins averaged $3.47 a barrel last week as compared to an average of under $1 in January.
